analysis:
Both changed files in this batch are documentation only: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/mlx-upstream-sync-2026-10-22.md, lines 1-5) and a docs/architecture/hardware-support.md edit (line 3 date bump, line 702 path correction for GatedDelta.swift). Neither change touches executable code, keys, attestation, coordinator protocol, authorization, encryption or cache storage, so I found no security regression and no invalidated threat assumption in the supplied evidence.

The changelog does describe a security-relevant change that is not visible here. libs/mlx, libs/mlx-swift, libs/mlx-swift-lm and the nested mlx-c move to new submodule pins, with SDK API changes (LanguageModel.prepare takes state and PrefillParameters, image/video payload moves to .source, Qwen 3.5 weight sanitizing can throw, and a new Generation.rejectedToolCall event). The Metal kernel sources change, so the release metallib changes. Pointer or source diffs for these were not supplied, so I could not review them.

Relevant threat-model items for the next pass:
- TB-007 and T-028: decrypted prompt and KV data in GPU memory.
- T-041: prefix-cache and SSD tier. Confirm that the new prepare/PrefillParameters API does not change cache salt scoping, DBK3 AAD or HMAC lookup-tag construction.
- T-008: confirm the provider still fails closed on encryption failure.
- T-013, T-034 and T-054: build identity changes with the new metallib and binary, so signed-artifact qualification must be refreshed. The platform side is outside this repo's scope.
- A throwing weight sanitizer and the ignored rejectedToolCall event are error-path behaviors to check for fail-open handling.

The moved-path claim at hardware-support.md line 702 (MLXLMCommon/GatedDelta.swift) is unverifiable from this batch. It is a documentation accuracy matter only. No finding is raised. Deeper review is warranted only for the submodule and provider source changes, which are outside the supplied units.
